answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation: each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and that deposit acts as a bridge between its past behavior and its future privileges. A newcomer starts in a barren stretch with no trust, and only sustained honest work lets it reach the oasis of full trading rights. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes expensive, because each clone needs its own locked stake, just as forging a rare pigment requires costly raw material for every batch — the attacker pays linearly per identity while honest agents pay once and reuse their reputation.
